newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan joins World Bank drive to help S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan joins World Bank drive to help S.Africa.

text.p: Taiwan's state-funded International Economic Cooperation Development Fund pledged on Friday to support the World Bank's US$67 million project to help South African businesses and exports.

Under a pact with the World Bank, the fund would provide technical assistance and know-how to small and medium-sized South African businesses to help boost the country's exports, but no financial help, said a fund official who asked not to be identified.
Taiwan said in the agreement it was prepared to provide financial assistance to South Africa but only if the World Bank asked, the official said.
"Taiwan's development fund has no plan to provide any part of the US$67 million programme, but we will consider it if World Bank requests," he said.

The International Economic Cooperation Development Fund was converted into an non-profit agency by Taiwan's Economic Ministry in earlier 1996. The fund lends to small and medium-sized enterprises in developing countries.
South Africa remains Taiwan's biggest ally and one of only 30 states that maintain diplomatic relations with Taipei rather than with Taiwan's longtime rival, China.
Vice-premier Hsu Li-teh visited South Africa in September and proposed a joint venture to build a US$3.5 billion petrochemical complex there.
Taipei's ties with Pretoria have become complicated in recent months as South Africa has expressed its willingness to establish diplomatic ties with China.
South Africa foreign minister Alfred Nzo made a high-profile fact-finding tour to Beijing in March.
South African trade ties with China have soared in recent years, fuelling pressure for for recognition.
South Africa has said no switch to Beijing was imminent.
